policy: Operationally relevant systems are reviewed across open-source, open-core, source-available, and proprietary source models; licensing is a visible classification, not an inclusion gate.

projects.name: Agno
projects.description: Python framework and AgentOS runtime for building, serving, observing, securing, and managing agent platforms.
projects.canonical_data: agent definitions, sessions, memory, knowledge, traces, evaluations, and application storage
strengths: Covers the full agent-platform path from SDK definitions to API runtime, UI, storage, traces, and deployment
Human approvals, JWT-based access control, memory, knowledge, evaluations, and observability are integrated
Large tool and interface ecosystem with MCP, A2A, messaging, and self-hosted deployment options
weaknesses: The broad SDK, runtime, UI, and deployment surface increases conceptual and upgrade complexity
Default telemetry requires an explicit opt-out for teams with strict outbound-data policies
Application teams still own tool safety, model behavior, infrastructure hardening, and cost controls
projects.why_it_matters: Shows what an integrated, self-hostable agent platform looks like when runtime operations are treated as part of the framework rather than an afterthought.

projects.name: Aider
projects.description: Mature terminal pair-programming agent built around Git-aware edits and broad model support.
weaknesses: Narrower tool surface than newer harnesses
Primarily an interactive pair programmer
projects.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that constrained, Git-native agency can be both useful and auditable.

projects.name: Browser Use
projects.description: Framework and agent runtime for controlling websites through browsers.
weaknesses: Websites remain nondeterministic
Cloud browser paths complicate data boundaries
projects.why_it_matters: A focused reference for agents acting through unstable visual environments.

projects.name: Claude Code
projects.description: Proprietary Anthropic coding agent for terminal, IDE, GitHub, and programmatic workflows.
projects.canonical_data: local working tree, project instructions, and resumable Claude Code sessions
projects.current_repo_note: The public repository is canonical, but the operational distribution remains proprietary under Anthropic commercial terms.
strengths: Strong repository-scale editing, shell use, and Git workflows
Granular permissions, hooks, MCP, subagents, and resumable sessions
Terminal, IDE, GitHub, and SDK surfaces
weaknesses: Operational implementation is proprietary and coupled to Anthropic models
Model processing is remote even though tools and files can remain local
projects.why_it_matters: A major provider-native reference for controlled coding agents and the runtime exposed through Claude Agent SDKs.

projects.name: Claude Agent SDK
projects.description: Provider-native Python and TypeScript SDKs that embed the Claude Code agent loop, tools, permissions, hooks, sessions, subagents, skills, plugins, and MCP.
projects.canonical_data: streamed SDK messages, Claude Code session state, project instructions, checkpoints, tool results, and application-defined external session stores
projects.current_repo_note: The Python repository is the representative open wrapper; the product also ships a commercially governed TypeScript SDK and bundles the Claude Code runtime.
strengths: Exposes the production Claude Code agent loop with built-in file, shell, web, MCP, subagent, skill, and plugin capabilities
Permissions, lifecycle hooks, human input, file checkpointing, session resume and fork, and OpenTelemetry support provide strong control seams
Python and TypeScript bindings let applications own orchestration while reusing a mature interactive coding-agent runtime
weaknesses: The runtime is provider-native and requires Anthropic models rather than a substitutable model backend
The MIT Python wrapper bundles a commercially governed Claude Code executable, while the TypeScript SDK is governed by Anthropic commercial terms
Powerful default file and shell tools require deliberate permission, sandbox, credential, and data-retention policy
projects.why_it_matters: Shows the tradeoff of embedding a mature provider-owned agent runtime: unusually deep tools and controls with materially less model and licensing portability than open provider-agnostic frameworks.

projects.name: Cline
projects.description: IDE-centered coding agent with approval-gated file, terminal, browser, and MCP tools.
weaknesses: IDE-centered workflow
Operator review remains the main safety boundary
projects.why_it_matters: A leading example of human control around autonomous coding tools.

projects.name: Codex
projects.description: Local coding agent for reading, changing, and running code from the terminal.
strengths: Terminal, IDE, SDK, and MCP surfaces
weaknesses: Best experience depends on hosted models
Long autonomous runs still require review
projects.why_it_matters: A reference implementation for controlled, tool-using coding agents.

projects.name: CrewAI
projects.description: Framework for coordinating role-based agents and structured multi-agent flows.
weaknesses: More agents can amplify nondeterminism
Debugging emergent handoffs remains difficult
projects.why_it_matters: A prominent test case for whether multi-agent structure improves outcomes enough to justify complexity.

projects.name: DB-GPT
projects.description: Agentic data assistant for planning and executing SQL, Python analysis, reusable skills, and multi-source reporting in sandboxed environments.
projects.canonical_data: database schemas, connected datasets, knowledge bases, skills, workflow state, and generated artifacts
strengths: Plans and executes multi-step SQL and Python analysis rather than stopping at query generation
Combines databases, files, knowledge bases, reusable skills, RAG, and multi-agent workflows
Supports sandboxed execution, self-hosting, local models, and OpenAI-compatible providers
weaknesses: The broad platform and deployment surface create substantial setup and operational complexity
Human approval and rollback behavior vary across agents, tools, and application flows
Reliable production analysis still depends on model quality and careful database permissions
projects.why_it_matters: A comprehensive reference for data agents that combine query generation, code execution, skills, sandboxing, and reports in one runtime.

projects.name: DeepSeek Harness
projects.description: Plugin-oriented agent runtime with event-sourced sessions, policy controls, workflows, and replaceable model and tool seams.
projects.canonical_data: append-only session events in JSONL or SQLite plus YAML configuration
strengths: Event-sourced sessions support persistence, replay, forks, search, and telemetry
Model, tool, storage, sandbox, and interface layers are replaceable plugins
Approvals, workflows, background jobs, and subagents are first-class runtime concepts
weaknesses: Upstream labels the project a developer preview with compatibility-breaking changes
The broad plugin surface creates substantial architectural and operational complexity
Some optional subagent integrations depend on separately licensed external runtimes
projects.why_it_matters: A rare open implementation of a durable agent harness where execution policy, event history, recovery, and extension seams are explicit runtime primitives.

projects.name: Devin
projects.description: Hosted autonomous software-engineering agent with an observable shell, IDE, browser, API, and parallel sessions.
projects.canonical_data: cloud workspaces, repository state, session history, knowledge, and playbooks
strengths: Long-running cloud workspaces expose shell, editor, browser, and logs
Human takeover, API access, parallel sessions, knowledge, and playbooks support team workflows
weaknesses: Proprietary managed service with limited implementation inspectability
Cloud execution and retained organizational context reduce data sovereignty
Official guidance still recommends bounded tasks and human review for reliability
projects.why_it_matters: A reference proprietary cloud agent for delegated, asynchronous software work rather than only interactive code assistance.

projects.name: DSPy
projects.description: Framework for programming and optimizing modular AI systems, including retrieval pipelines, tool-using ReAct agents, evaluation, and self-improving model programs.
projects.canonical_data: Python modules, declarative signatures, examples, evaluation sets, optimization traces, and compiled programs
strengths: Declarative signatures and modular programs separate system intent from brittle hand-written prompts
Evaluation-driven optimizers can improve prompts, examples, and weights against explicit metrics
Includes tool schemas and ReAct agent loops while remaining compatible with varied model backends
weaknesses: It is a general AI-programming framework rather than a full operational agent platform
Optimization requires representative datasets, metrics, model calls, and careful experimental discipline
Deployment, persistence, permissions, and production recovery remain application-defined
projects.why_it_matters: Broadens the Atlas beyond orchestration by treating AI-system behavior as typed, evaluable, optimizable programs.

projects.name: Gemini CLI
projects.description: Open-source terminal agent for coding, research, and tool-assisted workflows.
weaknesses: Centered on Gemini model access
Recovery and trace ergonomics are still evolving
projects.why_it_matters: Shows how a provider-backed terminal agent can remain extensible and open source.

projects.name: Google Agent Development Kit
projects.description: Google's open multi-language framework for tool-using agents, graph workflows, delegation, state, evaluation, human approvals, and local or managed deployment.
projects.canonical_data: code or declarative agent and workflow definitions, chronological session events, mutable state, artifacts, traces, and evaluation sets
projects.current_repo_note: The Python repository is the canonical metadata source for one ADK product also implemented by Google in TypeScript, Go, Java, and Kotlin; language feature parity varies.
strengths: Open, inspectable agent and workflow runtime with official implementations across five languages
Broad tool, MCP, OpenAPI, A2A, state, memory, evaluation, trace, and deployment seams
Callbacks, tool confirmation, workflow interruption, pause and resume, and session rewind provide strong control and recovery surfaces
weaknesses: Feature parity and maturity vary materially by language, with Python providing the deepest implementation
Gemini and Google Cloud are the best-integrated path even though model and deployment seams are replaceable
Major-version changes to agent APIs, events, and session schemas create migration risk in a fast-moving framework
projects.why_it_matters: A significant provider-published framework whose operational runner remains open and replaceable across model, storage, tool, protocol, and deployment seams.

projects.name: Goose
projects.description: Extensible local agent for coding and general computer tasks with MCP-based tools.
projects.current_repo_note: The project moved from block/goose to aaif-goose/goose.
weaknesses: Reliability varies by extension and model
Observability is less structured than graph runtimes
projects.why_it_matters: A practical model for local, protocol-extensible agents.

projects.name: GPT Researcher
projects.description: Autonomous research agent that gathers web sources and produces cited reports.
weaknesses: Source quality still needs human review
Long runs can be costly and difficult to steer
projects.why_it_matters: Separates research-agent evaluation from generic coding autonomy.

projects.name: GStack
projects.description: Cross-host AI engineering workflow with generated skills, browser automation, QA, security, release, and persistent-learning integrations.
projects.canonical_data: Git-versioned skills, plans, review and QA artifacts, browser evidence, and append-only learning records
projects.current_repo_note: Multi-host support is generated from a Claude-oriented canonical skill set; GBrain integration is adjacent and separately cataloged.
strengths: End-to-end, evidence-bearing delivery process from product framing through review, QA, release, and retrospection
Local browser automation, security review, verification gates, and recovery-oriented tooling
Generated support across ten coding-agent hosts plus pair-agent and cross-model review workflows
weaknesses: The large workflow and skill surface is strongly opinionated and requires deliberate adoption
The primary experience remains Claude Code-oriented despite generated multi-host support
A fast-moving main branch, no formal GitHub releases, and partial Windows support increase upgrade risk
projects.why_it_matters: Shows how structured roles, artifacts, safety gates, and verification turn general coding agents into a repeatable software-delivery system.

projects.name: Haystack
projects.description: Production-oriented Python orchestration framework for explicit RAG pipelines, tool-using agents, context engineering, evaluation, and lifecycle control.
projects.canonical_data: typed pipeline graphs, component state, documents, messages, tool calls, traces, and application-defined memory
strengths: Explicit pipelines, loops, branches, routing, retrieval, and agent steps make control flow inspectable
Lifecycle hooks, tool-call metrics, token accounting, evaluation, and tracing support production recovery
Broad provider, retrieval, storage, component, and deployment interoperability
weaknesses: Complex pipelines require more deliberate composition than higher-level opinionated agent APIs
Some serving, MCP, UI, and enterprise operations rely on adjacent Hayhooks or commercial products
Persistent memory and authorization policy remain application and integration concerns
projects.why_it_matters: A mature reference for transparent, production-oriented orchestration where retrieval and agent control flow remain explicit.

projects.name: Kiro
projects.description: Proprietary agentic IDE and CLI centered on specs, steering files, hooks, powers, and MCP integrations.
projects.canonical_data: local working tree plus Markdown specs, steering files, hooks, and service-managed sessions
projects.current_repo_note: Kiro's official GitHub repository is documentation and issue-tracking surface, not reusable operational source.
strengths: Specs and steering keep intent in reviewable project files
Hooks and powers support explicit repeatable automation
IDE, CLI, and MCP cover interactive and scripted workflows
weaknesses: Operational implementation is proprietary and governed by AWS service terms
Model and service processing limits local-only operation
projects.why_it_matters: A distinct provider product that makes specifications and durable project guidance first-class coding-agent artifacts.

projects.name: LangChain
projects.description: Model-portable Python framework with a prebuilt agent loop, composable tools, middleware, structured output, and durable LangGraph execution.
projects.canonical_data: application-defined graph state and message history
strengths: Prebuilt agent loop with composable model, tool, middleware, and structured-output seams
Broad first-party provider integrations and model portability
Durable execution, persistence, and human interruption through LangGraph
weaknesses: The abstraction surface and release cadence create meaningful upgrade overhead
Durability depends on the separate LangGraph package rather than a small standalone core
The strongest hosted observability and deployment paths are separate LangSmith services
projects.why_it_matters: A mature reference for a high-level, provider-portable agent API layered over a durable workflow runtime.

projects.name: LangGraph
projects.description: Graph-based runtime for durable, stateful, controllable agent workflows.
weaknesses: Framework complexity is substantial
Application quality depends on graph design
projects.why_it_matters: A benchmark for treating control, persistence, and recovery as runtime primitives.

projects.name: Letta Code
projects.description: Stateful agent harness with memory, identity, skills, schedules, subagents, and self-improvement.
projects.current_repo_note: The former letta-ai/letta repository is now a landing page; active code moved here.
weaknesses: Agent can rewrite its own context
Cloud features affect portability
Current codebase is much newer than historical repo
projects.why_it_matters: Defines embedded, self-editing agent memory and long-horizon runtime behavior.

projects.name: LlamaIndex
projects.description: Data and agent framework for ingestion, indexing, retrieval, tools, workflows, multi-agent applications, and document-centric AI systems.
projects.canonical_data: documents, nodes, indices, workflow events, messages, tool state, and application-defined stores
projects.current_repo_note: This entry represents the MIT-licensed LlamaIndex OSS framework; LlamaParse and LlamaCloud are separate commercial services.
strengths: Deep ingestion, indexing, retrieval, tool, workflow, and document-agent primitives in one ecosystem
Very broad integration catalog across models, embeddings, data sources, and storage backends
Supports high-level agent construction while preserving lower-level control over data and retrieval
weaknesses: The large package and integration ecosystem creates versioning, discovery, and maintenance overhead
Hosted parsing, extraction, indexing, and deployed-agent capabilities are separate commercial services
Application teams must design authorization, durable state, evaluation, and recovery policy
projects.why_it_matters: A foundational framework for data-intensive AI systems where retrieval, documents, structured data, and agents converge.

projects.name: Mastra
projects.description: Open-core TypeScript framework and runtime for tool-using agents, durable workflows, memory, delegation, evaluation, observability, and self-hosted or managed deployment.
projects.canonical_data: application-defined agents, tools, message and thread memory, workflow run state and snapshots, traces, evaluations, and storage records
projects.current_repo_note: The root license path map makes repository content outside ee/ Apache-2.0; every ee/ path is commercially restricted, and Mastra Platform is a separate proprietary service.
strengths: A configurable agent loop backed by typed tools, workflows, memory, scoring, and durable execution
Strong approval, suspension, resumption, tracing, replay, and failure-control surfaces
Broad model portability plus MCP, A2A, ACP, browser, sandbox, storage, and deployment integrations
weaknesses: The large, rapidly changing monorepo creates substantial conceptual and upgrade surface
Production authentication, authorization, Agent Builder, and other ee/ features have commercial restrictions
The documentation license page still broadly describes Mastra as Apache-2.0 despite the authoritative root license carving out every ee/ path
projects.why_it_matters: An unusually integrated TypeScript agent stack that treats tools, memory, workflows, evaluation, human control, observability, and deployment as one operational framework while exposing a clear open-core boundary.

projects.name: Microsoft Agent Framework
projects.description: Framework for building, orchestrating, and hosting agents with workflows and multi-agent patterns.
projects.current_repo_note: Microsoft identifies Agent Framework as the successor path for AutoGen and Semantic Kernel agent APIs.
weaknesses: Newer consolidated framework
Azure integrations can pull deployments toward one cloud
projects.why_it_matters: Represents the convergence of agent SDKs and durable workflow orchestration.

projects.name: Open Interpreter
projects.description: Local agent that uses code and shell execution to complete computer tasks.
projects.current_repo_note: The canonical repository is openinterpreter/openinterpreter.
weaknesses: Host execution increases risk
Less structured recovery than sandboxed runtimes
projects.why_it_matters: Makes the tradeoff between local control and host-execution safety especially visible.

projects.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
projects.description: Provider-agnostic Python agent framework with tools, handoffs, guardrails, resumable runs, sessions, tracing, MCP, and sandbox integrations.
projects.canonical_data: typed run items, resumable run state, and pluggable session stores
strengths: Small core abstractions cover tools, handoffs, guardrails, approvals, and resumable multi-agent runs
Pluggable sessions, tracing processors, model providers, MCP transports, and sandbox backends
Typed run items and explicit interruption state make execution inspectable and recoverable
weaknesses: OpenAI models and hosted tools remain the most complete and documented execution path
Provider adapters can expose uneven feature support across models
Some tracing, hosted tools, and sandbox paths send data to external services
projects.why_it_matters: Shows how a provider-published SDK can keep its operational loop open while exposing replaceable model, storage, tracing, and execution seams.

projects.name: OpenClaw
projects.description: Local-first personal agent runtime connecting models, tools, skills, schedules, devices, and messaging channels through one gateway.
projects.canonical_data: local gateway sessions, workspace files, skills, configuration, and channel state
strengths: Local gateway unifies sessions, tools, events, channels, and companion devices
Broad provider, channel, skill, plugin, and MCP interoperability
Schedules and persistent workspace state support proactive personal-agent workflows
weaknesses: Host tools and inbound messaging create a large security boundary
Safe multi-user exposure requires deliberate pairing, sandbox, and gateway configuration
Breadth increases operational and troubleshooting complexity
projects.why_it_matters: A prominent open personal-agent runtime whose durable gateway and communication surfaces go well beyond a single coding session.

projects.name: OpenCode
projects.description: Provider-flexible open-source coding agent with terminal and desktop interfaces.
weaknesses: Fast-moving interfaces can churn
Safety depends on configured tools and permissions
projects.why_it_matters: A strong benchmark for provider-neutral coding-agent design.

projects.name: OpenHands
projects.description: Self-hostable coding-agent platform and control center for interactive work and event- or schedule-driven automations.
projects.canonical_data: working trees, agent sessions, conversation events, and automation definitions
strengths: OpenHands agent plus Agent Canvas support self-hosted interactive and automated work
Agents can run on the host, in containers, on remote machines, or in managed cloud
ACP support allows alternate coding-agent backends
weaknesses: Running without a sandbox grants agent tools the host user's filesystem access
Multiple backends and automation integrations add deployment complexity
projects.why_it_matters: A major open alternative for observable coding agents and for operating several agent backends through one control surface.

projects.name: Pi
projects.description: Minimal, extensible terminal coding agent bundled with a multi-provider API, agent core, and TUI libraries.
projects.canonical_data: local working tree, JSONL sessions, extensions, prompts, and skills
strengths: Small agent loop with first-party libraries for models, state, and terminal UI
Extensions, prompts, skills, and themes make the harness deeply adaptable
First-class Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google model support
weaknesses: No built-in permission system for filesystem, process, network, or credentials
Safe use on untrusted repositories requires external containerization or sandboxing
projects.why_it_matters: A compact open coding-agent harness that exposes reusable runtime components instead of prescribing a large platform.

projects.name: Prime Agent
projects.description: Long-running coding and research harness built around persistent IPython, recursive subagents, durable state, and bounded autonomy.
projects.canonical_data: daemon-backed sessions, persistent IPython state, goals, memories, skills, and versioned harness refinements
strengths: Persistent Python control environment makes tools and context programmable
Recursive subagents, background sessions, schedules, goals, and heartbeats support long work
Harness refinements are bounded, evidence-backed, versioned, and reversible
weaknesses: Generated Python and commands run with the user's permissions rather than a security sandbox
Persistent and self-editing state demand careful inspection and trust boundaries
The project is new despite rapid adoption
projects.why_it_matters: A distinctive open harness for durable, recursively delegated agent work where lifecycle and recovery are first-class.

projects.name: Pydantic AI
projects.description: Typed Python framework for production agent applications, tools, graphs, and evaluation.
weaknesses: Python-focused
Runtime policy remains application-defined
projects.why_it_matters: Shows how software-engineering rigor can reduce agent uncertainty.

projects.name: smolagents
projects.description: Compact agent library centered on code agents, tool calling, and model portability.
weaknesses: Fewer durable-runtime primitives
Safety and persistence are largely application responsibilities
projects.why_it_matters: A useful counterpoint to heavier orchestration frameworks.

projects.name: Vanna
projects.description: User-aware SQL agent framework with executable database tools, permission-aware identity, tool memory, streaming UI components, and customizable lifecycle hooks.
projects.canonical_data: database schemas, tool-use memories, conversation state, permissions, and application-defined context
projects.current_repo_note: GitHub marks the repository archived; the reviewed Vanna 2.0 code and documentation remain available.
strengths: Executes and verifies SQL through explicit tools instead of returning text-only query suggestions
Propagates user identity and access groups through prompts, tools, and SQL filtering
Tool memory, custom tools, lifecycle hooks, and multiple model/database integrations are first-class
weaknesses: The public repository is archived, making its maintenance and successor path uncertain
Production safety depends on application-defined authentication, permissions, and database runner policy
The 2.0 rewrite increases migration cost for applications built on the older retrieval API
projects.why_it_matters: Demonstrates how a text-to-SQL agent can combine execution, learned examples, identity-aware permissions, and a production-facing interface.

projects.name: WrenAI
projects.description: Open-core generative-BI and text-to-SQL system with a governed semantic layer, validation tools, agent SDKs, MCP, and commercial agentic applications.
projects.canonical_data: Git-friendly MDL, instructions, query examples, and optional local semantic memory
projects.current_repo_note: The current open-core product separates its Apache-licensed engine and SDKs from commercial Agentic Mode, GenBI UI, security, and enterprise deployment features.
strengths: Semantic modeling, dry-plan validation, row limits, and structured errors make query correctness explicit
Apache-licensed CLI, MCP server, agent SDKs, and connectors support local and framework-driven workflows
Business definitions, query examples, and context remain human-reviewable and Git-friendly
weaknesses: The autonomous Agentic Mode, GenBI UI, access controls, and advanced deployment features are commercial
The open SDKs rely on an external agent framework or client to own the reasoning loop
Operating a governed semantic layer adds modeling and maintenance work before analysis
projects.why_it_matters: A strong example of data-agent reliability built from governed context, validation, recoverable errors, and explicit open-core boundaries.

projects.name: Amazon Quick
projects.description: AWS work assistant combining organizational knowledge, research, analytics, actions, custom agents, skills, and scheduled workflows.
projects.canonical_data: service-managed conversations, spaces, organizational indexes, knowledge graph, agent configurations, and workflow artifacts
projects.current_repo_note: Amazon Quick is the current product boundary that evolved from QuickSight; it also integrates Amazon Q Business indexes and capabilities.
strengths: Combines enterprise search, cited research, analytics, applications, and actions in one governed workspace
Custom agents, scheduled work, MCP and OpenAPI connections, and human-in-the-loop automation cover broad work patterns
Permission-aware organizational data and AWS administration provide a strong enterprise control boundary
weaknesses: Proprietary managed service with limited implementation inspectability
The broad product bundle and evolving desktop preview make capability boundaries and maturity uneven
Organizational context and long-term personalization are service-managed rather than local-first
projects.why_it_matters: A major hyperscaler reference for an enterprise assistant that unifies knowledge, agent creation, business actions, analytics, and persistent work context.

projects.name: ChatGPT
projects.description: OpenAI's general-purpose assistant for conversation, files, research, connected applications, memory, projects, and tool-using work.
projects.canonical_data: service-managed conversations, saved memory, projects, connected-app context, tasks, and generated work artifacts
projects.current_repo_note: This record covers the end-user ChatGPT product; Codex and OpenAI Agents SDK remain distinct operational systems.
strengths: Broad, mature assistant experience spanning research, files, creation, connected applications, and tool-using work
Projects, saved memory, recurring tasks, and cross-device clients support continuity across sessions
Strong usability, documentation, and ecosystem adoption
weaknesses: Operational implementation and model runtime are proprietary and provider-native
Capabilities, limits, retention controls, and available tools vary by plan and change frequently
Service-managed context and memory reduce data portability and local control
projects.why_it_matters: A reference general assistant whose product boundary now includes durable context, connected data, research, scheduled work, and consequential tool use—not only text chat.

projects.name: Claude
projects.description: Anthropic's consumer assistant for conversation, projects, files, research, connected applications, artifacts, and cross-chat memory.
projects.canonical_data: service-managed conversations, editable memory entries, project knowledge, connected-app context, files, and artifacts
projects.current_repo_note: This record covers the Claude Free, Pro, and Max end-user product; Claude for Work, Claude Code, and Claude Agent SDK have distinct operational and contractual boundaries.
strengths: Projects, project knowledge, cross-chat search, and editable memory provide strong continuity with visible user controls
Research combines iterative web and connected-app retrieval with citations and explicit steering
Files, artifacts, connected applications, and memory import/export support broad knowledge-work workflows
weaknesses: The operational implementation and model runtime are proprietary and provider-native
Memory, research, integrations, and usage limits vary by plan and rollout stage
Service-managed context and project knowledge are not local-first despite export and deletion controls
projects.why_it_matters: A leading general assistant reference for explicit projects, inspectable memory controls, connected research, and portable user context within a polished conversational workspace.

projects.name: DeepSeek
projects.description: DeepSeek's hosted web and mobile assistant with synchronized conversations, reasoning modes, web search, and file upload.
projects.canonical_data: service-managed account, synchronized chat history, uploaded files, and generated responses
projects.current_repo_note: This record covers the proprietary DeepSeek Web and App product; open model weights, the API platform, DeepSeek Harness, and downstream deployments are separate boundaries.
strengths: Reasoning and non-reasoning modes cover both concise conversation and more deliberate problem solving
Web search, file upload, text extraction, and cross-platform history provide a practical general-assistant baseline
Free web and mobile access makes the hosted product unusually accessible
weaknesses: The assistant service is proprietary even though separate DeepSeek model releases use open-weight licenses
Durable projects, editable extracted memory, connectors, and broad action integrations are not documented
Service-managed data and limited operational transparency constrain governance and portability
projects.why_it_matters: A significant provider-native assistant whose open-weight model ecosystem and proprietary hosted product must be represented as separate licensing and operational boundaries.

projects.name: Gemini Apps
projects.description: Google's general assistant for conversation, files, Deep Research, connected applications, personalization, Gems, and scheduled or multi-step work.
projects.canonical_data: service-managed conversations, activity, personalization, Gems, notebooks, connected-app context, files, schedules, and generated artifacts
projects.current_repo_note: This record covers Gemini Apps for individual users; Gemini in Workspace, Gemini Enterprise, Gemini CLI, Google ADK, and the Gemini API remain distinct products.
strengths: Deep Research can combine web, file, Gmail, Drive, and NotebookLM sources with an editable research plan
Connected Apps, Gems, personalization, schedules, and multi-step mobile actions span a broad assistant surface
Activity, personalization, exports, and connected-app controls provide meaningful user management options
weaknesses: The operational implementation and model runtime are proprietary and Google-native
Capabilities and data treatment vary across personal, work, school, plan, region, and experimental surfaces
The breadth of overlapping Google AI products makes the individual Gemini Apps boundary easy to conflate with Workspace or enterprise offerings
projects.why_it_matters: A leading ecosystem assistant that joins web research, personal Google context, reusable Gems, multimodal creation, and scheduled or multi-step actions.

projects.name: Microsoft Copilot
projects.description: Microsoft's personal AI companion across web, desktop, mobile, and selected Microsoft surfaces, with files, creation, search, memory, and multi-step tasks.
projects.canonical_data: service-managed conversations, activity history, personalization, uploaded files, connected Microsoft context, tasks, and generated content
projects.current_repo_note: This record covers consumer Microsoft Copilot under its individual-use terms; Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio, Security Copilot, GitHub Copilot, and Azure agent services remain distinct products.
strengths: Broad availability across standalone apps, web, Windows, mobile, and conversations embedded in other Microsoft surfaces
Files, creation, web-grounded answers, personalization, and multi-step tasks support varied everyday work
Dedicated Copilot terms and privacy controls make the consumer product boundary more explicit than the wider Copilot brand
weaknesses: The Copilot brand spans many separately governed products, making capability and data-boundary communication difficult
Features, models, integrations, and memory behavior vary by account, subscription, platform, and region
The operational implementation is proprietary and service-managed with limited portability
projects.why_it_matters: A major consumer assistant reference whose reach across Microsoft devices and applications is operationally distinct from the enterprise Microsoft 365 Copilot product.

projects.name: T3 Chat
projects.description: Multi-model chat workspace with provider choice, persistent and temporary threads, attachments, profiles, and optional web search.
projects.canonical_data: service-managed threads, attachments, profiles, preferences, and generated chat artifacts
projects.current_repo_note: T3 Chat is the hosted assistant product; the separately open-source T3 Code control plane is a coding-agent workflow candidate.
strengths: First-class choice across several major model-provider ecosystems
Clean persistent and temporary chat workflows with attachments and reusable profiles
Simple interface lowers the friction of comparing and switching models
weaknesses: Bounded search and tool calls do not provide the autonomous work loop of a general agent
Hosted proprietary service with limited implementation and storage inspectability
Tool and enterprise-integration breadth is narrower than larger assistant platforms
projects.why_it_matters: A useful comparison point for assistant products whose primary value is a consistent multi-provider workspace rather than owning a model or autonomous runtime.

projects.name: Z.ai
projects.description: Z.ai's hosted GLM assistant for conversation, file input, deliberate reasoning, model selection, and integrated coding work.
projects.canonical_data: service-managed account, chat history, uploaded files, preferences, and generated conversation or coding artifacts
projects.current_repo_note: This record covers the hosted chat.z.ai assistant surface; Z.ai's API services, ZCode product boundary, and separately licensed GLM model releases require independent review.
strengths: A low-friction hosted assistant exposes model selection, file input, and deliberate reasoning without requiring API setup
The integrated ZCode entry point connects general conversation with a more focused coding workflow
The public product exposes current terms, privacy information, and chat-history management
weaknesses: Public product documentation does not yet establish durable projects, extracted memory, rich connectors, or broad action tools
The relationship among chat.z.ai, ZCode, API services, and separately released GLM models requires careful boundary maintenance
Hosted internals and data portability are limited, and operational evidence is thinner than for more established assistants
projects.why_it_matters: A notable GLM-native assistant and useful coverage point for an ecosystem that is underrepresented by directories focused only on US provider products.

projects.name: ActivityWatch
projects.description: Privacy-focused automatic activity and time tracking.
weaknesses: Captures activity metadata, not meaning
Needs downstream synthesis
Can still expose sensitive behavior
projects.why_it_matters: Broadens ambient capture beyond screenshots: app and time telemetry can become evidence for work recall.

projects.name: AnythingLLM
projects.description: Local-first AI workspaces, RAG, agents, and broad model/provider support.
weaknesses: Knowledge remains app-centric
Provenance and temporal truth are limited
Can become a generic AI shell
projects.why_it_matters: Demonstrates low-friction, provider-agnostic local AI over personal sources.

projects.name: AppFlowy
projects.description: Open-source collaborative workspace combining documents, databases, tasks, and AI.
weaknesses: Heavy system to customize
AI memory lifecycle is not first-class
Database-centric canonical data
projects.why_it_matters: Shows how structured workspaces and approachable UX can coexist with user control.

projects.name: Basic Memory
projects.description: Markdown-native knowledge graph and semantic memory bridge for AI clients.
weaknesses: MCP can add tool/context overhead
Graph semantics are lightweight
Sync and mobile are more complex locally
projects.why_it_matters: The clearest human-readable bridge between personal knowledge and multiple agents.

projects.name: Chroma
projects.description: Developer-oriented embedding database for AI applications.
weaknesses: Not a second brain by itself
Requires ingestion, governance, provenance, and UX layers
projects.why_it_matters: Included as a building block so vector storage is visible without being mistaken for a product category.

projects.name: Cognee
projects.description: Knowledge-graph and memory platform for persistent agent context.
weaknesses: Complex pipeline surface
Less transparent canonical memory
Temporal semantics are weaker than Graphiti
projects.why_it_matters: Represents knowledge-graph enrichment and memory pipelines across heterogeneous data.

projects.name: Foam
projects.description: VS Code-based personal knowledge management using Markdown and wikilinks.
weaknesses: VS Code-centric
Limited structured memory lifecycle
No built-in AI memory
projects.why_it_matters: Represents the smallest viable local-first graph: Markdown, links, editor, and Git.

projects.name: GBrain
projects.description: Local-first agent memory service with Git-versioned Markdown, hybrid retrieval, typed knowledge graphs, synthesis, citations, gap analysis, and MCP access.
projects.canonical_data: Git-versioned Markdown brain repositories, with PGLite or Postgres retrieval projections, typed links, citations, and durable background-job state
projects.current_repo_note: The Git repository is the canonical project and install source; the unrelated npm package named gbrain is not this system.
strengths: Git-versioned Markdown remains the system of record while PGLite or Postgres provides hybrid lexical, vector, and graph retrieval
Synthesis, citations, gap analysis, contradiction checks, consolidation jobs, and durable agent-facing memory operations go beyond raw chunk search
Local CLI, stdio and HTTP MCP, broad model and embedding providers, and self-hosted deployment preserve strong portability
weaknesses: The very broad CLI, server, graph, job, skill, evaluation, and integration surface creates meaningful setup and upgrade complexity
Semantic retrieval, extraction, synthesis, and some ingestion paths depend on optional external model or SaaS providers
The project is young and changing quickly despite strong adoption, extensive tests, and unusually detailed operational documentation
Some enrichment paths need paid model services, and durable subagent loops remain Anthropic-specific
projects.why_it_matters: Combines human-owned, Git-versioned memory with production-oriented retrieval, graph, synthesis, provenance, and agent integration in one local-first system.

projects.name: Graphiti
projects.description: Temporal context graph engine for evolving agent knowledge.
weaknesses: Operational graph-database burden
LLM-dependent extraction
Not a user-facing brain
projects.why_it_matters: Supplies the strongest model for changing truth, provenance, and as-of retrieval.

projects.name: Joplin
projects.description: Offline-first Markdown notes and tasks with end-to-end encrypted sync.
weaknesses: Weak graph semantics
AI is not the architectural center
Sync complexity remains
projects.why_it_matters: Contributes mature offline-first, encryption, sync, and import/export lessons.

projects.name: Khoj
projects.description: Self-hostable AI second brain over documents, web, agents, and automations.
weaknesses: Canonical knowledge is not human-readable
Large application surface
Temporal contradictions need stronger governance
projects.why_it_matters: The closest complete open-source AI second-brain product in the set.

projects.name: LangMem
projects.description: Utilities for extracting and managing long-term memories in agent applications.
weaknesses: Framework coupling
Not a user-facing product
Smaller ecosystem than Mem0
projects.why_it_matters: A useful example of memory as explicit application logic rather than a full platform.

projects.name: Logseq
projects.description: Privacy-first graph-oriented knowledge management and collaboration.
weaknesses: New database architecture adds migration risk
Can overwhelm casual users
AI remains an add-on
projects.why_it_matters: Contributes durable user-controlled knowledge, backlinks, blocks, and graph-native thinking.

projects.name: Mem0
projects.description: A universal long-term memory layer for AI agents.
weaknesses: Canonical memory is not human-readable
Extraction can encode model errors
Managed platform outpaces OSS features
projects.why_it_matters: Defines the external-memory service pattern and a strong retrieval baseline.

projects.name: Memos
projects.description: Lightweight, Markdown-native, self-hosted quick capture.
weaknesses: Limited graph and memory intelligence
Not agent-native
Best for fragments rather than deep synthesis
projects.why_it_matters: A reminder that capture friction matters more than elaborate ontology at the moment of thought.

projects.name: Milvus

weaknesses: Not a second brain by itself
Requires ingestion, governance, provenance, and UX layers
projects.why_it_matters: Included as a building block so vector storage is visible without being mistaken for a product category.

projects.name: Open Notebook

weaknesses: Primarily source-set oriented
Long-term identity and memory are limited
Less suited to operational life management

weaknesses: High privacy and storage risk
Noisy raw evidence
Project activity is slower than leaders

projects.name: Qdrant
projects.description: High-performance vector similarity search engine.
weaknesses: Not a second brain by itself

projects.why_it_matters: Included as a building block so vector storage is visible without being mistaken for a product category.

projects.name: Quivr
projects.description: Opinionated RAG framework for integrating generative AI into applications.
weaknesses: Less of a personal knowledge product
Temporal memory is weak
Requires product engineering around it
projects.why_it_matters: A representative vector-centric RAG system and useful contrast to graph/temporal memory.

projects.name: Reor
projects.description: Private local AI PKM using Markdown, local models, and vector search.
weaknesses: Repository is archived
Desktop-centric architecture
Limited temporal/provenance model
projects.why_it_matters: A valuable example of local AI over Markdown, but also a warning about project continuity.

projects.name: SilverBullet
projects.description: Markdown-based programmable personal productivity platform.

AI and memory extraction are not central
Mobile experience is indirect
